_meta.description: Printed leaves the upstream OCR delivered twice, dropped from the served corpus by scripts/drop_duplicate_leaf.py. Each entry cites the scan page that proves the duplication, and lists every run of 3+ consecutive words in the dropped row that the kept row does not have, so what is lost is enumerated rather than assumed.

volumes.basis:
Migne PG118 pages 21 and 22 arrive twice in our OCR, as loci 21-22 and again as loci 23-24. Read from the scan (Internet Archive item patrologia.graeca.org, _118.zip): page 21 (cols 21-22) prints Η ΤΩΝ ΕΠΙΣΤΟΛΩΝ ΥΠΟΘΕΣΙΣ ΔΙΑ ΙΑΜΒΩΝ opening Ὁ Παῦλος ὁ αὐλὸς ἐκ τῶν πραγμάτων, which is loci 21 and 23 alike; page 22 (cols 33-34) prints Τούτου μέχρι γράφει δέ in its left column and Ἀλλ᾽ οὖν μανεὶς ἀνεῖλεν Ὀκταουίαν in its right, which are the openings of loci 22 and 24 respectively, and closes with Ἐῤῥωσθε, which is where locus 22 ends. Page 23 prints ΚΕΦΑΛΑΙΑ ΤΩΝ ΠΡΑΞΕΩΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΠΟΣΤΟΛΩΝ, which is our locus 25, so the loci after the duplicate run two behind the pages.

The second read of page 22 walked the columns in a different order, so loci 22 and 24 score only 0.482 on the similarity gate carve_cgpg_volume.py uses for rescanned leaves and were never shed. That is why the gate here is vocabulary rather than similarity.

drops.page_evidence: both are Migne PG118 page 21, cols 21-22, the iambic hypothesis of the epistles

both are Migne PG118 page 22, cols 33-34. Locus 22 reads the columns in printed order and ends on the page's last word Ἐῤῥωσθε; locus 24 reads them in another order and breaks off mid-word. Only 36 of locus 24's 546 words are absent from locus 22's vocabulary, and the single run of three or more is the same display head garbled differently, ΟΠΙΝ ΒΙΕΑΟΝ ΕΠΛΝΟΡΘΩΣΑ against ΟΠΠΝ ΒΙΒΑΟΝ ΕΗΑΝΟΡΘΟΣΑΣ for Ο ΤΩΝ ΒΙΒΛΩΝ ΕΠΑΝΟΡΘΩΣΑΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΝΑΓΙΝΩΣΚΟΥΣΙ.

volumes.basis:
Six consecutive pages of the Vita S. Clementis arrive twice, as loci 605-610 and again as 613-618. The EARLIER copy is the stray and the later one is the page in sequence, which is the opposite of what the candidate list's column order suggests, so it is spelled out here.

Read from the scan (Internet Archive item patrologia.graeca.org, _126.zip): page 605, cols 1197-1198 under the running head VITA S. CLEMENTIS BULGARIAE ARCHIEP., opens πάσχων πρὸς τοὺς θείους ἄνδρας, ὃ Μωϋσῆς πρὸς Θεόν, which is our locus 612, so a locus is its page plus seven. That page ends καὶ φωτὶ, and both locus 605 and locus 613 open φῶς προσλαβὼν εἰς οὐρανοὺς μετέστη, so both hold page 606; only 613 sits where page 606 belongs, directly after 612.

The text agrees. Locus 618 ends τὸν Υἱὸν παρεισ and 619 opens Πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται, continuing one Filioque argument, while 610 ends the same way and 611 opens on an unrelated new section. Loci 604 and 611 are not duplicates of 612 and 619 (containment 0.021 and 0.026), so the duplicated run is exactly these six pages and no more.

volumes.basis:
Two pages of the 2 Corinthians catena arrive twice, as loci 519-520 and again as 521-522. The EARLIER copy is the stray, and here that is settled from the bytes rather than from the scan, because the two copies do not end alike: locus 520 breaks off mid-word at Οὐκ ἀλλαχοῦ κατ- and the row that follows it in the file, 521, opens a different lemma, so that copy's sentence is never finished. Locus 522 ends Οὐκ ἀλλαχοῦ καταισχυνθῶμεν, and locus 523 opens ἀλλὰ ἐν μόνῃ τῇ περὶ τῆς ἐλεημοσύνης καυχήσει, completing it. So 521-522 sit in reading order and 519-520 are the duplicate.

No printed page is cited for this one. The volume's loci have drifted several pages ahead of the scan by this point (scan page 521 is still 2 Cor 8:1-8 while these loci are at 8:21), and locating the leaf would take more page fetches than the evidence needs: the vocabulary gate below shows the dropped copy holds nothing the kept one lacks, so the worst case is that a duplicate rendering goes rather than a duplicate leaf.

drops.page_evidence: no page located; direction established from the file, where locus 520 breaks off mid-word and 522 completes the sentence into 523

volumes.basis:
Two pages of Palamas' homilies arrive twice, as loci 159-160 and again as 163-164. The earlier copy is the stray, settled from the file by two independent signals rather than from the scan.

First, truncation: locus 159 breaks off at ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἀπὸ παραδείνμα· while 163 carries the word whole, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἀπὸ παραδείγματος. Second, the join: locus 164 ends Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν, παρ᾽ ὑμῖν and locus 165 opens μένων· ὁ δὲ Παράκλητος, τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, which completes John 14:25-26 across the row boundary, while locus 161, which follows 160, opens on unrelated matter.

No printed page is cited. The route that would have made pages cheap is closed: the Internet Archive's per-volume text layers (patrologiaecursu<NNNN>mign) recognized only Migne's Latin column and contain no Greek at all, 0 Greek characters in 3 MB for PG118, so a row cannot be matched to a page through them. Locating this leaf by image would mean hunting the drift by hand: pages 154 and 160 of the scan are Homilies XXII and XXIII at columns 293-294 and 305-306, nowhere near these loci.

drops.page_evidence: no page located; direction from the file, where 159 is truncated mid-word and 164 completes John 14:25-26 into 165

volumes.basis:
Two pages of Zonaras' Epitome arrive twice, as loci 633-634 and again as 635-636. The earlier copy is the stray.

What does NOT decide it, and is worth saying because it decided the last two leaves: the join test is useless here. Loci 634 and 636 end with the same words (Εὐφημίαν μετονομάσας), and 633 and 635 open with the same words, so 632 joins to either opening and either ending joins to 637. Both hypotheses survive.

What decides it is the vocabulary gate, which is asymmetric on this pair: dropping 634 costs nothing, while dropping 636 would lose text, so 636 is the fuller reading. Reading the two confirms which: 636 has Ἐν τοῖς χρόνοις τούτου γέγονε σεισμὸς φοβερώτατος where 634 has γέγι «ὸς φοβερώτ, and 636 gives the regnal figure ἐπὶ μησὶ τρισίν where 634 garbles it to κπι. The 633/635 pair is clean in both directions and follows the same choice.

No printed page is cited, for the reason recorded on the PG151 entry: the Internet Archive text layers hold no Greek, and the loci drift too far from the scan's page numbers to find a leaf cheaply by image.

drops.page_evidence: no page located; direction from the vocabulary gate, which allows dropping the earlier copy and refuses the later, and from the later copy carrying the readings the earlier garbles
